huakui.name: HANSUN Huakui 11
huakui.full: HANSUN Huakui 11 (China Beauty 11), Ethiopia Guji Hambella, Heirloom, Customized Natural
huakui.note: Two 200 g batches roasted back to back on Nov 15 with the same first-crack target: curve A develops for a shorter time at a faster rate, curve B longer and slower.

Switch.name: Hario V60 Neo Switch
Switch.material: Tritan (PCT resin) cone, resin switch, silicone base
Switch.method: Close the valve, pour and steep, then open the valve and let it drain fully.
Switch.notes: Hario sells it as the Switch & Match NEO set: a V60 Dripper NEO cone on a Switch base, and the cone also works on its own. From Nov 17 it sits on two scales, so the beverage flowing out is logged too.

Hoop.name: Ceado Hoop
Hoop.type: Flat-bottom percolation; a top ring spreads the water over the bed
Hoop.method: Pour into the ring and let it shower onto the bed.
Hoop.notes: Without stirring, extraction stayed around 13 to 15%. Stirring pushed it to about 20% but clogged the filter (one brew dripped for 8 minutes).

V60.name: Hario V60 (ceramic)
V60.notes: The ceramic body pulls the slurry temperature down quickly at first, then holds heat better than the resin Switch once it is warm.

coffee-watch.name: Coffee Watch
coffee-watch.role: Runs every brew: reads both scales and the refractometer over Bluetooth and the bed probe through a wired input, computes extraction yield, and uploads one record per brew to Dropbox.
specs: JSON record per brew, plus a 10 Hz curve CSV from Nov 10

bed-probe.name: Bed probe
bed-probe.role: Sits in the slurry and gives the temperature curve on every brew card.
specs: 100K NTC thermistor in a 3 mm 316L stainless tube

difluid.name: DiFluid RS Extract
difluid.role: Measures the TDS of every cup; Coffee Watch receives the reading and computes extraction yield.

bookoo.name: Bookoo Themis Ultra
bookoo.role: Main scale under the brewer; tracks the water poured.

ck811.name: Lefu CK811BLE
ck811.role: Lower scale under the server; tracks the beverage flowing out.

c40.name: Comandante C40
c40.role: Main hand grinder; usually 24 clicks for the Switch.

phantox.name: MAVO Phantox Pro
specs: 120 clicks per turn, about 16.7 µm per click

roasts.label: Limu batch 2
roasts.note: Stored mixed with the other Oct 31 roasts later on.

roasts.label: Gotiti Nov 4
roasts.note: Development flattened toward the end. Same-day cupping: roasted nuts and hazelnut, a little barley tea, thin; sweetness grew as it cooled.

roasts.label: Gotiti Nov 6 #1
roasts.note: Fan cut at 7:00 sped up the approach to first crack; flat stretch 8:05 to 9:05, then a late surge to 212 °C. Stored mixed with batch 2.

roasts.label: Gotiti Nov 6 #2
roasts.note: Fan locked at about 51%; slow, steady development to 212.5 °C. Stored mixed with batch 1; a faint rubbery smell on day 1.

roasts.label: Gotiti Nov 6 #3
roasts.note: First crack was not marked (estimated 7:50 to 8:00). Heater and fan glitched around 8:35, then the bean temperature surged to about 218 °C. A faint rubbery smell on day 1.

roasts.label: Gotiti Nov 6 #4
roasts.note: 300 g was too much for the heater: it stayed at full power from 7:00 to drop. The lightest batch of the day and no rubbery smell.

roasts.label: Syrina A
roasts.machine: Cardputer Roast on a DIY fluid-bed
roasts.note: Dropped by the app's 206 °C auto-drop protection, which was then turned off. RoR collapsed about 20 s before first crack.

roasts.label: Syrina B
roasts.machine: Cardputer Roast on a DIY fluid-bed
roasts.note: Ran 107 s past first crack instead of the planned 55 s; RoR crashed at first crack like A.

roasts.label: Syrina C
roasts.machine: Cardputer Roast on a DIY fluid-bed
roasts.note: Manual heat from about 185 °C: the beans stalled for about 30 s, then RoR held near 20 through first crack.

roasts.label: Syrina D
roasts.machine: Cardputer Roast on a DIY fluid-bed
roasts.note: Dropped by temperature at 209 °C after 24 s of development.

roasts.label: Syrina F
roasts.machine: Cardputer Roast on a DIY fluid-bed
roasts.note: The roast log was not uploaded, so only the marks are known. First roast on the reworked controller; no RoR crash.

roasts.label: Syrina X1
roasts.machine: Cardputer Roast on a DIY fluid-bed

roasts.label: Syrina X2
roasts.machine: Cardputer Roast on a DIY fluid-bed
roasts.note: 150 g on curve F (the log recorded 100 g green by mistake).

roasts.label: Syrina Nov 15 (204.5 g)
roasts.machine: Cardputer Roast on a DIY fluid-bed
roasts.note: The last Syrina batch, 204.5 g on curve F.

roasts.label: Huakui B
roasts.machine: Cardputer Roast on a DIY fluid-bed
roasts.note: Curve B: longer, slower development. Cupped right after roasting: clearly sweeter and fuller, nutty and floral.

roasts.label: Huakui A
roasts.machine: Cardputer Roast on a DIY fluid-bed
roasts.note: Curve A: shorter, faster development. Cupped right after roasting: thinner, a little bitter.

brews.method: Stirred throughout; the final drawdown was slow.

brews.note: Flat and muted. Faint sourness as it cools, with peanut, roasted-barley grain and a slightly green edge.

brews.method: 30 g dose with 500 g water. Last drops measured 0.69% TDS.

brews.note: Too dilute overall.

Two-stage: closed-valve steep, then the last 100 ml poured with the valve open. Leftover liquid 1.15% TDS.

brews.note: Sharp sourness and slight bitterness with a nutty aftertaste; the finish stays sour and mouth-drying.
brews.method: Switch base with a V60 Neo cone. Two-stage with stirring: 100 g steeped for 1 min and drained, then the valve closed and the rest of the water added.

brews.note: Less sharp sourness than the two-stage cup; bitterness stays in the finish.
brews.method: All water at once to 1:16, valve opened at 2:00, done at 3:00. Last drops 1.58% TDS.

brews.note: The sharp sourness turned into rounder acidity, little green character, less mouth-drying; but one-dimensional, like lemon water.
brews.method: Same as the previous cup at 1:17, with stirring. Leftover liquid 1.41% TDS.
Evaluation recipe: 1:16 with stirring, 4:00 total. Last drops 1.59% TDS.

brews.note: Bright acidity and clear sweetness; a clean cup with no off-flavors.
brews.method: Stirred; fines clogged the filter and it dripped for about 8 minutes.

brews.note: A little thin at this extraction. Creamy sweetness, smoky, with a touch of chocolate and toffee.
The roasted-barley note from cupping is gone; short aftertaste, and the orange from the bag notes is missing.
brews.method: Immersion at 1:15.

brews.note: Slightly bitter with a mouth-drying finish.
brews.method: Stirred throughout; the drain slowed and the brew ran to 5:00. A/B pair with the next cup.

brews.note: Much better than the stirred cup: no noticeable bitterness or mouth-drying.
brews.method: No stirring; done at 3:00. A/B pair with the previous cup.
Deliberately strong ratio at low extraction, for fun. 1 g dried osmanthus added with the grounds (it raises the TDS reading); Shuke filter paper.

brews.note: A standout cup: pronounced sweetness, soft and gentle, light acidity, no mouth-drying, clean.
brews.method: Stirred.

brews.note: Preferred over the 1:16 cup brewed right after it.

brews.note: Less preferred than the 1:17 cup brewed just before it.

brews.note: No sharp sourness; orange and jasmine, but the aroma is a little faint.

brews.note: Hot: sour and mouth-drying with a sweet aftertaste. Below about 52 °C the drying eases into lemon-like acidity with sweetness; strawberry, raspberry, stone fruit.

1:14, one 5 s stir at about 1:00, valve opened at 1:30, drained by 2:30.
Same recipe as the El Tambo cup before it: 1:14, one short stir, valve opened at 1:30.

brews.note: Slightly bitter and mouth-drying.

brews.note: Strongly sour and mouth-drying; no burnt bitterness and no nutty notes.
Enjoyable.
Enjoyable.
Quite sweet and soft.
brews.method: Stirred before the valve opened at 2:00; no stirring after.

brews.method: Drained until no liquid showed above the bed, then closed the valve.

Aiming for high TDS at low extraction: cooler water and 1:14.

brews.note: Good.

brews.note: More acidic than earlier cups; now a fairly typical Gesha profile.

Good; the best of the four cups that morning.
Complex but still a little mouth-drying; not enjoyable.
